overall_summary: Deduplicating 47 unique shorts reveals a distinct performance divide: experiential second-person cosmic survival scenarios ('What If You Fell Into...') and counterintuitive extreme planetary benchmarks consistently drive the highest views (800-1,050+ views) and strongest like ratios (3.5% to 4.5%). In contrast, passive psychology hooks ('Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories') and duplicate/re-uploaded trivia concepts ('Why Space Is Completely Silent') show severe algorithmic fatigue, stagnating under 100 views.

winning_patterns.pattern: Second-Person Extreme Environment Survival ('What If You Fell Into...')
winning_patterns.evidence: 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (1,029 views, 38 likes) and 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (972 views, 18 likes) vastly outperformed the channel baseline.
winning_patterns.action: Anchor space and science content around experiential second-person stakes where the viewer must physically survive a bizarre cosmic or planetary phenomenon.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'Venus Has a Day Longer Than Its Year' generated 981 views and 21 likes rapidly within recent weeks; 'The Planet Darker Than Coal' reached 1,027 views and 36 likes.
winning_patterns.action: Leverage stark, concrete comparative hooks that contradict everyday sensory intuition within the first 1.5 seconds.

weak_patterns.evidence: Multiple iterations of 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' flatlined at 5, 10, and 53 views; 'Your Brain Is Hiding This From You' produced only 38 views.
weak_patterns.action: Halt generic text-based psychology trivia unless driven by an urgent narrative mystery or dramatic real-world experiment.

weak_patterns.pattern: Repeated Concept Re-Uploads with Static Hooks
weak_patterns.evidence: Three distinct uploads of 'Why Space Is Completely Silent' plateaued between 34 and 220 views with near-zero engagement growth.
weak_patterns.action: Eliminate near-identical re-uploads of evergreen trivia; prioritize novel entities and uncharted physical anomalies.
